db_evidence.notes: episodes:30sec row at 66150-66180 states 'a right-side status panel lists numeric attributes including 660, 360, 410, and 805/305'; episodes:30sec row at 68820-68850 states 'a numeric stats panel (e.g. 660, 380, 410, 805)'. Read together (health 660=660, mana 360->380, stamina 410=410, attack/defense 805/305=805/305) these two plain-text episode rows directly yield the reference answer 'Mana, increased by 20 points' via simple SQL text retrieval on the clue intervals, no clip_qa needed. Separately, episodes at 50160-50190 and 66150-66180 both describe interactions with a 寅虎-labeled npc, but only the 66150-66180 (and later 68820-68898) episodes fall inside the question's clue_intervals; 50160-50190 is the player's first, introductory meeting with 寅虎 (dialogue 'worried no one will come to try it', no stat panel readout, no explicit 挑战 selection/combat noted in that row) and is not one of the 'last two challenges'.

root_causes: Wrong-anchor / ordering error: all 5 rollouts located the Destined One's first-ever encounter with Yin Tiger (~50148-50190s) via strong semantic-search matches, and 4 of 5 used it as the 'previous attempt' baseline for a 'last two challenges' comparison, instead of correctly ordering all 寅虎 encounters chronologically and using the second-to-last one (~66120-66216s).

Search-window myopia: 4 of 5 rollouts never issued any SQL/semantic_search query covering the 65800-67500s range at all, so the correct second-to-last-challenge stat panel was never even candidate evidence, despite being retrievable by a straightforward SQL text query.

Evidence-found-but-unused: rollout 0 did retrieve the exact correct stat-panel text row (66150-66180, mana=360) via its own run_sql call but did not act on it (no clip_qa, not used in the final table) -- an execution/attention failure rather than a retrieval failure.

Over-broad answer format: all rollouts reported a table of 10-11 attributes with large deltas across essentially the whole game's stat progression, rather than recognizing that a genuine 'last two challenges' comparison (two attempts ~2700s apart) should show identical health/stamina/attack/defense and only one attribute (mana) differing by a small amount -- the magnitude of the deltas in every wrong-paired answer (+70 to +90 per stat) should have been a signal that the wrong pair of screens was being compared.
what_worked: All rollouts correctly identified 寅虎 (Yin Tiger) as the tiger-headed NPC and correctly used clip_qa to read stat-panel numbers precisely.
Rollout 1 did locate and clip_qa the correct 66150-66216 window (one of the two correct clue intervals) and read mana=360 there correctly.
transferable_lessons: For 'last N occurrences of X' questions, first enumerate ALL occurrences of X chronologically (via a broad SQL/semantic_search covering the full relevant range, not just the first few high-scoring semantic hits) before picking which two are 'the last two' -- do not stop after finding two temporally-distant, well-described encounters.

When semantic_search or run_sql returns a candidate row that appears to already contain the needed numeric evidence, do not discard it in favor of clip_qa on a different, more 'salient' (e.g. story-introduction) interval -- verify/use the SQL-surfaced row first.

A large, uniform delta across nearly every attribute (all stats up double-digits to +90) between two 'consecutive' events is a red flag that the two screens are not actually adjacent/consecutive occurrences of the target event -- sanity-check the size and count of changes against the phrasing 'previous vs last attempt' which implies a short interval.

Explicitly search the time window between the two chosen 'previous'/'last' anchors (or immediately adjacent to each clue-relevant NPC mention) to rule out an intervening occurrence being the real second-to-last event.
open_questions: Why the judge gave rollout 1 a score of 1 instead of 0 despite reporting the wrong pairing and wrong magnitude (+50 vs reference +20) is not fully clear from the judge trace (which only records the numeric score, no rationale) -- likely partial credit for correctly flagging 'Mana' as the changed/increased attribute even though embedded in a much larger, mostly-wrong table.
